elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement, including all Service Option Attachments, for convenience.

elements.element: Customer may exercise the termination-for-convenience right on 30 days' prior notice.
elements.evidence: Customer may terminate by providing at least thirty (30) days' prior notice, without waiting for a calendar month-end.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly requires prior written notice to IBM.

elements.element: Vendor must refund prepaid fees attributable to the period after the effective termination date.
elements.evidence: IBM must refund prepaid charges for the period after the effective date of termination; 'prepaid charges' is substantively equivalent to prepaid fees.

elements.element: The refund must be calculated on a pro-rata basis.
elements.evidence: The refund provision expressly requires calculation on a pro-rata basis.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right effective during a committed term.
elements.evidence: IBM receives no mid-term convenience-termination right. Its only stated convenience-based termination right is effective at the end of the then-current Service Option Attachment term.
The clause expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: The required Customer notice period is between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The operative minimum notice period is thirty (30) days, not 60–90 days. Customer's ability to elect to give longer notice does not change the contractual notice requirement.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee charged to Customer does not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The clause imposes no early-termination fee, so no fee exceeds the permitted cap.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience effective at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Either party, including IBM, may elect to terminate a Service Option Attachment at the end of its then-current term.

elements.element: Vendor may not make a convenience termination effective before the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The only stated IBM convenience-based termination right is tied to the end of the then-current term; no mid-term right is granted.

elements.element: Vendor must provide at least 90 days' prior notice of its end-of-term termination.
elements.evidence: The renewal provision requires written notice at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term.

result.reason: The redline fully reaches the preferred position: Customer has a 30-day written-notice convenience right, receives a pro-rata refund of post-termination prepaid charges, and IBM has no mid-term convenience right. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its required Customer notice period is 60–90 days, while the clause requires only 30 days. The redline preserves the prerequisite-attachment carveout, IBM's transition-period duties, and the renewal framework. It is not minimal because it unnecessarily relocates the renewal paragraph and awkwardly reorders the termination sentence. Drafting quality is also reduced by the dangling 'and' after subsection (a), which suggests an omitted additional condition.
